label: <DEL> step (stronger when the sequence starts with g/p/q/e/2) + original-phase e
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit. The <DEL> step holds 62% of activation mass and fires on 32% of delimiter steps (6.4x lift), and every top activation is at <DEL>. Whether it fires there depends strongly on the first original token: rate is about 2-2.5x higher when the sequence starts with g, p, q, e or 2, and lower when it starts with i, 3, s, t, u or y. A second component is an input of e during the original phase (30% rate, 21% of mass). It also fires weakly in the original phase on h, n, o and r, more so at late positions (t = 7-9) of long sequences, which often build up toward the <DEL> peak. It is nearly silent during the copy phase (7.6% of mass, 0.4x lift). Plain delimiter-or-e covers 83% of mass at 36% precision; adding the first-token condition raises precision to about 0.60 but recall stays near 0.54, so the rest of the delimiter-step variation is not captured.
